decision.selected_method: finite joint passive structure performance search

input.expected_observation: At least one legally constructed proposal completes both frozen loading directions through recovery and reduces low and recovery tip speed, monitor speed, generalized velocity, drift, and static-balance residual relative to candidate_1775, ideally below the frozen qualification thresholds, while retaining low displacement at least 0.006 m, high displacement at most 0.025 m, recovery residual at most 0.002 m, stiffness ratio at least 1.5, bilateral slack-to-taut recruitment, legal routing, and zero contacts.
input.fixed_conditions: Keep candidate_1775's four-segment, four-tendon topology, four 0.072 m lengths, whole-chain spans, routing, payouts, tendon properties, load histories, passive no-active-control treatment, timestep, and all original thresholds fixed. Search only legal material and circular-section coordinates within the declared finite bounds, using both original loading directions and matched frozen initialization.
input.hypothesis: The matched local evidence in result_35 weakens distal density and radius as sufficient small-step fixes: lowering distal density produced only a very small symmetric reduction in low and recovery motion, while increasing distal radius slightly worsened those motions. A larger joint backbone retuning over Young's modulus, density, circular radius, and retained near-maximum bending viscosity may shift modal frequency and damping enough to reduce low-stage and recovery motion while preserving the already observed bilateral displacement, progressive stiffness, tendon recruitment, routing, and no-contact margins. This is joint design exploration and performance optimization; any result is attributed to the complete tested backbone design, not to one parameter.
input.interpretation: Result_35 shows that a 1 kg/m^3 distal density decrease slightly reduced speeds and imbalance, whereas a 10 micrometre distal radius increase slightly worsened them; the joint point was nearly additive and remained far from qualification. Because those perturbations were too small and the complete task objective was invalidated by stage qualification, they do not support a strict gradient or a single-coordinate edit. A finite joint search with larger but bounded changes has higher information value than repeating tiny local stencils.
input.stopping_condition: Stop this request after at most ten proposals and eight complete finite-time evaluations. Then inspect the best complete result: diagnose and materialize a supported design if one approaches qualification while preserving mechanism margins; otherwise revise toward another physically distinct branch such as segment-length distribution or tendon engagement timing rather than extrapolating this finite neighborhood.
input.weakening_observation: The hypothesis is weakened if all evaluated joint material-section proposals either leave low and recovery motion essentially unchanged, worsen those diagnostics, lose displacement or stiffness-ratio margins, eliminate bilateral recruitment, or violate routing/contact constraints. A finite negative result will bound only this declared neighborhood and will not establish structural infeasibility.
